digest.component_or_area: enrichment queue and ticket digest event storage
propositions: Physical deletion of committed UUID events reclaims no repository space and breaks cross-clone reconvergence via rename detection pairing, without solving the actual problem which is read cost
The queue reduction is latest-wins per event type and filenames encode monotonic timestamps, enabling a newest-first suffix read that bounds file opens to O(3+k) instead of O(history) per ticket
Read cost is asymmetric: digest_sidecar is already O(1) file opens, but _events_of opens every matching file, causing pending_enrichment to exceed its 20ms budget at 404-544ms on the live tracker
Any merge-safe retention scheme must rename to a deterministic source-derived path with identical content, not pair a deletion with a fresh-UUID add

The design bounds reads without adding retention, deletion, or renaming committed events, preserving invariant I1 and achieving byte-identical reconvergence regardless of whether the optimization is applied
